subject: Re: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics — routing & MOP

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heathrow-analytics.com>

Cc: Peter Liu <peter.liu@heathrow-analytics.com>

Subject: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the prefix caching examples. Before we kick off the pilot, we need to clarify account ownership and co-sell mechanics so both teams are aligned. We currently have three target accounts in scope: Heathrow Logistics (pilot), BlueDock (prospect), and TransitEdge (renewal conversation).

Questions from our side:
- Which accounts will Redwood own vs. our team as the ISV partner?
- How will inbound leads be routed (partner-sourced vs. direct)?
- What does success/look like for the pilot (who owns expansion conversations)?

We'd like a short mutual action plan (MOP) and a single point of contact on each side. Can you send a proposed account map and routing rules by early next week?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Partnerships
Heathrow Analytics

Attachments: none (will share their internal list after mapping)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heathrow-analytics.com>
Cc: Peter Liu <peter.liu@heathrow-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics

Hi Samira — great to meet you and glad the demo helped.

I've drafted an initial account map and routing proposal and attached an editable spreadsheet (Heathrow-Account-Map_v1.xlsx). High level proposal:
- Heathrow Logistics (pilot): partner-led co-sell. Heathrow Analytics AE will own initial outreach; Redwood to provide solution architect support and joint exec briefing.
- BlueDock (prospect): hybrid — partner-sourced but Redwood AE takes lead on procurement/contracting.
- TransitEdge (renewal): Redwood-managed due to existing enterprise contract; partner invited for technical handoff and joint upsell.

Proposed routing rules (draft):
- Partner-sourced inbound leads -> tag as PARTNER_SOURCE; route to partner AE + CC Redwood AE for 10 business days.
- Post-demo, responsibility for expansion follows the owner who closed the commercial deal unless otherwise agreed in MOP.

I'll loop in our alliances and sales ops to finalize. Attaching: Heathrow-Account-Map_v1.xlsx and a working MOP template (CoSell-MOP_v0.3.pdf).

Next step: internal review at Redwood, then we'll send a one-page MOP for you to sign off.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Heathrow-Account-Map_v1.xlsx (workbook), CoSell-MOP_v0.3.pdf (draft)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heathrow-analytics.com>, Peter Liu <peter.liu@heathrow-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics — routing proposal

Team — forwarding Samira's note and my draft account map. Need quick alignment so we can get the MOP signed and start the pilot the week of July 5. Key asks:
1) Confirm ownership recommendation below (pilot + routing rules).
2) Approve the routing SLAs and crediting approach so we can put numbers into the MOP.
3) Any compliance or procurement blockers for TransitEdge (they're an enterprise renewal).

My suggested splits (from my earlier note):
- Heathrow Logistics (pilot) = Partner-led co-sell (partner AE primary; Redwood provides SA + platform credits).
- BlueDock (growth prospect) = Hybrid (partner sources lead; Redwood AE handles commercial close).
- TransitEdge (enterprise renewal) = Redwood-owned; partner receives technical enablement role.

Routing SLA (draft): partner-sourced leads routed -> partner AE + CC Redwood AE within 1 business day; Redwood AE has 10 business days to assert commercial ownership by logging opportunity in Salesforce with partner role noted. If no entry by day 10, ownership defaults back to partner for that lead.

Credit / economics (proposal): referral credit to partner on first paid year if partner is listed as source; co-sell credit for expansion where partner actively engaged. We can model specific percentages after ACV estimates.

Attachments: Heathrow-Account-Map_v1.xlsx; CoSell-MOP_v0.3.pdf

Please reply with any redlines — Sergio, Camila, Ben: quick takes?

—Laura
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heathrow-analytics.com>, Peter Liu <peter.liu@heathrow-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics — routing proposal

Short notes from GTM:
- Routing SLA looks reasonable but we need explicit SLA for technical enablement handoff (SA assigned within 3 business days of pilot kickoff).
- Crediting: agree on referral credit; propose a simple table in the MOP mapping credit % by ACV band (0-100k = 8%; 100-500k = 6%; >500k = 4%).
- For TransitEdge (renewal) we should require a written waiver if partner wants to be listed as co-sell (they can be technical partner only). This avoids future disputes.

I can approve the pilot approach as long as finance signs off on the referral credit model. Also suggest offering Heathrow Analytics a one-time 10% discount for pilot customers (timeboxed to 90 days) to accelerate proofs.

Sergio
VP, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Operational notes:
- I'll add the partner domain routing rule into the partner-routing doc and push to production rules next week. Rules: partner_domain match -> auto-tag PARTNER_SOURCE; exclude domains listed as Redwood-enterprise (TransitEdge domain).
- Recommend a 30-day pilot observation window (not 14) for behavioral routing metrics — gives us more signal on who engages post-demo.
- I'll also add a check-box on the opportunity form to record 'Partner Engagement Level' (0/1/2) so crediting is auditable.

Ben — please confirm we have capacity to support a 3-business-day SA SLA for the pilot. If not, we should push back on the timeline to avoid poor experience.

Camila
Director, Sales Ops

Subject: Re: Co-sell account demarcation for Heathrow Analytics — routing & MOP (ACTION)

Hi Samira / Peter — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Summary of agreed plan (please confirm by reply):

1) Account ownership splits (agreed):
   - Heathrow Logistics (pilot): partner-led co-sell. Heathrow AE primary; Redwood provides SA and platform credits.
   - BlueDock (prospect): hybrid. Partner sources; Redwood AE manages commercial close.
   - TransitEdge (renewal): Redwood-owned; partner participates on technical handoff only.

2) Routing + SLAs (agreed):
   - Partner-sourced leads -> auto-tag PARTNER_SOURCE; route to partner AE + CC Redwood AE within 1 business day.
   - Redwood AE must log opportunity in Salesforce within 10 business days to assert commercial ownership.
   - SA assigned for pilot within 3 business days of kickoff.
   - Pilot observation window: 30 days, then review metrics and attribution.

3) Economics (draft):
   - Referral credit on first paid year (tiered by ACV as proposed). We will send the finance model for sign-off.
   - One-time 10% pilot discount to accelerate proof-of-value, timeboxed to pilot customers.

Next steps:
- Please confirm you accept the three items above. Once confirmed I will: (a) upload the finalized MOP to the DocuSign link below, (b) add Heathrow Analytics as a partner in the routing system, and (c) schedule a kickoff call for July 6 to introduce SA and GTM owners.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-def
Account map (editable): https://redwood.gdrive/partners/heathrow-account-map

If you confirm by EOD Tuesday we can keep the July 6 kickoff.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
